1.3.15|धातुभ्यः.explain: गतिहिंसार्थेभ्यः is itself an adjective (roots meaning motion or injury); the commentary simply names the noun it describes, roots (धातुभ्यः), since this whole rule is about verbs.

1.3.16|धातोः.explain: उपपदात् needs a noun to go with it; the commentary supplies धातोः (root) because this rule, like the one before it, is about verbs taking or not taking आत्मनेपद.

2.3.35|तृतीया.explain: The Bālamanoramā says the sūtra's च reaches back and pulls in तृतीया from an earlier, non-adjacent rule, the same way it pulls in पञ्चमी.

3.2.164|गमः.explain: गत्वर is an irregularly formed (निपातन) word; the commentary just names which root it is built from, गम् (to go) — that is not borrowed from another sūtra.

4.1.30|ङीप्.explain: The Bālamanoramā states outright that ङीप् continues here by anuवृत्ति from the earlier rule संख्याव्ययादेर्ङीप्.

4.1.32|ङीप्.explain: The Kāśikā says ङीप् is not newly stated here but is 'already accomplished' (सिद्धः) simply because the word ends in न् — exactly the condition of ऋन्नेभ्यो ङीप् (4.1.5).
4.1.32|ङीप्.quote: ङीप् च प्रत्ययः, स तु नकारान्तत्वादेव सिद्धः

4.1.35|ङीप्.explain: The Kāśikā says ङीप् 'is obtained anyway' (लभ्यते एव) from an earlier rule — this sūtra only adds that it is obligatory and changes पति to पत्नी.
4.1.35|ङीप्.quote: ङीप् तु लभ्यत एव। पूर्वेण विकल्पे प्राप्ते वचन

4.1.38|ङीप्.explain: The Bālamanoramā explicitly lists ङीप् among the words continuing by anuवृत्ति into this rule, along with ऐ च and उदात्तः.

4.1.39|ङीप्.explain: The Bālamanoramā explicitly says वा and ङीप् both continue here by anuवृत्ति from the earlier rules.

4.3.102|छन्दसि.explain: The Kāśikā says छन्दसि is drawn in by anuवृत्ति from the later rule शौनकादिभ्यश्छन्दसि (4.3.106).

5.1.15|चतुर्थीसमर्थात्.explain: The Bālamanoramā itself flags this as a filled-in ellipsis ('...न्तात् इति शेषः') — the standard reading that a thing's purpose is expressed by the 4th case, not a word borrowed from a numbered rule shown here.

5.1.99|तृतीयासमर्थात्.explain: The Kāśikā opens by saying 'तेन इत्येव' — the word तेन (and so the 3rd-case condition) continues here by anuवृत्ति from an earlier rule.

5.2.41|अस्य.explain: The Bālamanoramā states outright, 'तदस्य इति अनुवर्तते' — अस्य continues here by anuवृत्ति from an earlier rule.

5.2.42|अस्य.explain: The Kāśikā opens with 'तदस्य इत्येव' — अस्य is carried on here by anuवृत्ति, the same word noted for the previous sūtra.

5.2.53|डटि.explain: The Kāśikā opens 'डट् इति एव' — डट् (hence डटि, its locative) continues here by anuवृत्ति from an earlier rule that taught it.

5.3.117|स्वार्थे.explain: No special meaning is named for अण्/अञ् here, so by the standard convention the suffix is simply read in the sense of the base word itself (स्वार्थे).

6.1.12|छन्दसि भाषायां च.explain: The sūtra only lists the three words; the Kāśikā adds, on its own reading, that they are निपातन 'अविशेषेण' (without restriction) — i.e. in both Vedic and the classical language.

6.1.131|पदस्य.explain: The Kāśikā says explicitly that पद continues by anuवृत्ति from एङः पदान्तादति (6.1.109).

6.1.161|आदिः.explain: The Kāśikā explains that this word 'अनुदात्तस्य' is read with आदिः because, on its own, 'अन्त' (not आदि) would already be the default reading from context — a deliberate choice, not a borrowed word.

6.1.195|धातोः.explain: उपदेशे (in the original root-list) inherently concerns roots; the Kāśikā simply names धातवः as what is being talked about, not as a word fetched from a different numbered rule.

6.1.195|उपदेशे.explain: The Kāśikā opens 'उपदेशः इति वर्तते' — उपदेशे continues here by anuवृत्ति from an earlier rule.

6.3.26|पूर्वपदस्य.explain: A compound-internal replacement rule like this one targets the first member (पूर्वपद) by default unless told otherwise; the Kāśikā simply states it that way, not as a word fetched from elsewhere.

6.3.88|यति.explain: The Bālamanoramā explains the Siddhānta-kaumudī's 'इत्येव' as meaning this condition 'continues by anuवृत्ति alone' (अनुवर्तते एव).

6.3.116|पूर्वपदस्य.explain: A compound-internal lengthening rule like this one targets the first member (पूर्वपद) by default; the Kāśikā simply states it so, not as a word fetched from a numbered rule shown here.

6.4.37|अनुनासिक.explain: The Siddhānta-kaumudī says outright that 'अनुनासिक' here is read with its 6th-case ending dropped (लुप्तषष्ठीकम्), as a qualifier of वनति and the तनादि roots — the commentary's own construal of the sūtra's own word, not an anuवृत्ति.

6.4.82|धातोः.explain: The Bālamanoramā says धातोः continues by anuवृत्ति, picked out separately from the dvandva 'श्नुधातुभ्रुवाम्' in the earlier rule (अचि श्नुधातुभ्रुवां य्वोरियङुवङौ, 6.4.77).

6.4.83|धातोः.explain: The Bālamanoramā says the whole previous rule एरनेकाचः (6.4.82) continues here except एः itself — so धातोः carries forward from it too.

7.2.69|छन्दसि.explain: The Kāśikā says this निपातन 'is understood to be Vedic' (छन्दसि इदं निपातनं विज्ञायते) because in ordinary language the word would be सेनिवांस instead — the commentary's own inference from usage, not a borrowed word.

8.1.26|आदेशाः.explain: आदेशाः is simply the commentary's standing name for the class of substitutes (वाम्, नौ, त्वा, मा, ते, मे, etc.) taught a few rules earlier, used here as their collective label rather than a word fetched by anuवृत्ति.

4.1.31|ङीप्.explain: ङीप् runs on in this stretch, from 4.1.26 संख्याव्ययादेर्ङीप् — बालमनोरमा on 4.1.30: “ङीबित्यनुवर्तते”

4.1.36|ङीप्.explain: ङीप् runs on in this stretch, from 4.1.26 संख्याव्ययादेर्ङीप् — बालमनोरमा on 4.1.38: “ङीबिति चानुवर्तते”

4.1.37|ङीप्.explain: ङीप् runs on in this stretch, from 4.1.26 संख्याव्ययादेर्ङीप् — बालमनोरमा on 4.1.38: “ङीबिति चानुवर्तते”

5.1.100|तृतीयासमर्थाभ्याम्.explain: the 3rd-case समर्थ (तेन) runs on from the previous sūtra — काशिका on 5.1.99: “तेनेत्येव”

5.1.121|भावप्रत्ययाः.explain: the suffixes of the bhāva section opened at 5.1.119 तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ — काशिका on 5.1.121: “इत उत्तरे ये भावप्रत्ययाः”

6.1.63|छन्दसि.explain: commentators differ: some carry छन्दसि here, others apply the rule generally, since पद and the rest are used in ordinary language too — काशिका on 6.1.63: “केचिदत्र छन्दसीत्यनुवर्तयन्ति। अपरे पुनरविशेषेणेच्छन्ति”

6.1.194|अभ्यस्तानाम्.explain: runs on from 6.1.189 अभ्यस्तानामादिः, as the Kaumudī reads it — SK on 6.1.194: “अभ्यस्तानामादिरुदात्तो वा णमुलि परे”

6.4.26|नकारस्य.explain: the न runs on from 6.4.23 श्नान्नलोपः through 6.4.24 — काशिका on 6.4.26: “उपधाया नकारस्य लोपो भवति”
